extraction.name: Towards VQA Models That Can Read
extraction.description: This paper introduces the TextVQA dataset to facilitate progress on Visual Question Answering (VQA) models that can read text in images. TextVQA contains 45,336 questions on 28,408 images that require reasoning about text to answer, addressing limitations of existing datasets which either have a small proportion of text-related questions or are too small.
extraction.creator: Amanpreet Singh, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah, Yu Jiang, Xinlei Chen, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Marcus Rohrbach
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The TextVQA dataset was collected using a three-stage crowd-sourcing pipeline. In the first stage, annotators identified and filtered out images without text from the Open Images v3 dataset, resulting in 28,408 images. In the second stage, 1-2 questions were collected for each image, requiring annotators to provide questions whose answers necessitate reading text in the image. In the third stage, 10 ground truth answers were collected for each question.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: In some cases, the OCR system was unable to detect text, resulting in 0 OCR tokens for approximately 1,500 images. These cases were manually verified to actually contain text.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were sourced from the Open Images v3 dataset [27]. Categories with a higher likelihood of containing text (e.g., “billboard”, “traffic sign”, “whiteboard”) were prioritized for sampling based on an initial OCR analysis.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were pre-filtered by running the Rosetta OCR system to compute the average number of OCR boxes per category, which were then used as weights for sampling images from Open Images v3. A three-stage crowd-sourcing pipeline was used: first, annotators identified and removed images without text. Second, questions were collected with instructions to ensure they required reading text. Third, answers were collected with quality control measures, including removing questions where a majority of workers flagged them as poor quality (e.g., no text, not a question, unanswerable) and filtering bad annotators using hand-crafted questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For each image, 1-2 questions were collected. Annotators were instructed to provide questions that required reading text in the image, allowing for inferred or paraphrased answers. For a second question, annotators were asked to provide a different text-reasoning question with a different answer. Each question-image pair received 10 ground truth answers from humans. Annotators were given quality instructions and options to flag poor quality data (e.g., 'no text in image', 'not a question', 'unanswerable').
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A custom annotation interface was used for the three-stage data collection pipeline. Screenshots of the interface and detailed instructions are provided in Appendix A.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: To ensure answer quality, annotators were given instructions similar to those used in VQA and VizWiz datasets. Poor quality data was caught by providing annotators four options: (i) no text in image; (ii) not a question; (iii) answering the question doesn’t require reading any text in image; and (iv) unanswerable. Questions where a majority of workers marked any of these flags were removed. Hand-crafted questions with known correct answers were used to identify and filter out bad annotators. All 10 annotators agreed on the most common answer for 22.8% of questions, while 3 or more annotators agreed for 97.9% of questions.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 10 ground truth answers per question-image pair.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset addresses a critical need for visually impaired users, as studies have shown that a dominant class of questions asked by them on images of their surroundings involves reading text in the image. This work aims to endow VQA models with the ability to read text in images, which is important for assistive devices for the visually impaired.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset does not have significant biases with respect to images and questions, as indicated by low validation accuracies for 'Question Only' (8.09%) and 'Image Only' (6.29%) baselines.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The diversity of the answer space, involving brand names, cities, people’s names, time, and countries, makes it difficult to have a fixed answer space. The OCR system used is not perfect and fails at detecting text that is rotated, unstructured (e.g., a scribble), or partially occluded. The current model can only copy a single OCR token, but the dataset contains Q/A pairs requiring multiple OCR tokens in the correct order. There is a large gap between model performance and human performance (85.01%) and the upper bound achievable with OCR tokens (67.56%), suggesting room for improvement.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The TextVQA dataset is intended to facilitate progress on Visual Question Answering (VQA) models that can read and reason about text in images. It is suitable for training, validation, and testing of such models. It is also expected to encourage research on improving text detection and recognition in unconstrained environments.
